translations.text: The Lord called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting, saying:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When any of you brings an offering to the LORD, you must bring your offerings from the livestock, either from the cattle or from the sheep and goats.

If his offering is a burnt offering from the cattle, he must offer a male without blemish. He must bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting and present it before the LORD so that it may be accepted on his behalf.
He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and it will be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him.
He must slaughter the young bull before the LORD. The priests, Aaron’s sons, must present the blood and splash it against all sides of the altar at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He shall skin the animal for the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
The priests, Aaron’s sons, shall put fire on the altar and pile wood on the fire.
The priests, Aaron’s sons, must arrange the pieces, the head, and the fat on the wood that is on the fire on the altar.
He must wash its entrails and legs with water, and the priest must burn all of it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If his offering is from the flock, from the lambs or goats, as a burnt offering, he must offer a male without blemish.
He must slaughter it at the base of the altar, on its north side, before the LORD. The priests, Aaron’s sons, must splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
He must cut up its limbs, its head, and its fat, and the priest must arrange them on the wood that is on the fire on the altar.
He must wash its entrails and legs with water. The priest must present all of it and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If his offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he must bring his offering to the LORD from the turtledoves or young pigeons.
The priest must bring it to the altar, wring off its head, and burn it on the altar. He must drain its blood against the wall of the altar all around.
He shall remove its crop with the food in it and throw it beside the altar on the east side, in the place for the ashes.

He must split it open between its wings without separating it into two parts. The priest must burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
When someone brings a grain offering to the LORD, his offering must be fine flour. He must pour oil on it and put frankincense on it.

He must bring it to the priest, a son of Aaron. The priest must take a handful of the fine flour and oil, together with all the frankincense [?], and burn its memorial portion on the altar, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy portion of the LORD’s offerings.
When you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it must be of fine flour: unleavened cakes [?] mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers mixed with oil.
If your offering is a grain offering prepared on a griddle, it shall be unleavened fine flour mixed with oil.
Break it into pieces and pour oil over it. It is [?] fine flour.
If your offering is a grain offering prepared in a pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
You must bring the grain offering made from these things to the LORD and present it to the priest, and he must offer it on the altar to the LORD.
The priest shall set aside the memorial portion from the grain offering and offer it up on the altar, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons, a most holy portion of the Lord’s offerings.
No grain offering that you bring to the LORD may be made with yeast, because you must not burn any leaven or any honey as an offering to the LORD.
You may present them to the Lord as offerings of firstfruits, but they shall not be offered up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
You must season every grain offering of yours with salt. You must not leave the salt of your God’s covenant out of your grain offering. You must offer salt with all your offerings.
If you bring an offering of firstfruits to the LORD, you must bring ears of grain roasted in the fire, crushed and cleaned kernels, as your firstfruits offering.
You shall put oil and frankincense on it. It is an offering.
The priest shall offer up its memorial portion from the crushed grain and the oil, together with all the frankincense, as an offering to the Lord.
If his offering is a sacrifice of well-being, and he offers it from the cattle, he must offer a male or female without blemish before the LORD.
He must lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the tent of meeting. The priests, Aaron’s sons, must sprinkle the blood against all sides of the altar.
From the sacrifice of well-being he must present an offering to the LORD: the fat covering the entrails and all the fat on the entrails.
He must also prepare the two kidneys and the fat on them at the flanks, and the lobe of the liver together with the kidneys.
The priests, Aaron’s sons, must burn it on the altar, on the burnt offering and on the wood that is on the fire, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If his offering is from the flock, as a burnt sacrifice to the Lord, he must offer a male or female without blemish.
If he presents his offering from the lambs, he shall present it before the Lord.
He must lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it before the Lord at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons must sprinkle its blood all around the altar.

From the burnt sacrifice he must present an offering to the Lord: its fat and its entire fat tail, which he must remove close to the loins, the fat covering the internal organs, and all the fat on the internal organs.
He must also remove the two kidneys and the fat on them near the flanks, and the lobe of the liver along with the kidneys.
The priest shall offer it up on the altar as food, an offering to the Lord.
If his offering is a burnt offering from the goats, he shall present it before the Lord.
He must lay his hand on its head and slaughter it before the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons must sprinkle its blood all around the altar.
From it he must present his offering, an offering to the Lord: the fat covering the internal organs and all the fat on the internal organs.
and the two kidneys with the fat on them at the flanks. He shall remove the lobe of the liver along with the kidneys.
The priest shall offer them up on the altar as food, an offering with a pleasing aroma. All fat belongs to the Lord.
This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations, wherever you live: you shall eat neither fat nor blood.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When someone sins unintentionally by doing any one of the things that the Lord’s commandments forbid:
If the anointed priest sins, bringing guilt upon the people, he must offer to the Lord a young bull without blemish as a sin offering for the sin he has committed.
He must bring the bull to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, before the Lord, lay his hand on the bull’s head, and slaughter the bull before the Lord.
The anointed priest must take some of the bull’s blood and bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest must dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before the Lord, in front of the curtain of the sanctuary.

The priest must put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense before the Lord in the Tent of Meeting. He must pour out all the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
He must separate all the fat from the bull of the sin offering: the fat covering the internal organs and all the fat on the internal organs.
He must also remove the two kidneys and the fat on them near the flanks, and the lobe of the liver along with the kidneys.
Just as it is removed from the bull sacrificed as a burnt offering, the priest must offer these up on the altar of burnt offering.
The bull’s hide and all its flesh, together with its dung, its head, its legs, and its internal organs—
He must take the whole bull outside the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are deposited, and burn it on wood over the fire. It must be burned where the ashes are deposited.
If the whole congregation of Israel goes astray, and the matter is hidden from the congregation’s eyes, and they do any one of the things that the Lord’s commandments forbid and become guilty,
and the sin they have committed becomes known, the whole congregation must offer one young bull as a sin offering and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.
The elders of the congregation must lay their hands on the bull’s head before the Lord, and they must slaughter the bull before the Lord.
The anointed priest must bring some of the bull’s blood to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest must dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, in front of the curtain.

He must put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that is before the Lord in the Tent of Meeting. He must pour out all the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
He shall separate all its fat from it and offer it up on the altar.
He must do with this bull as he did with the bull of the sin offering; he must do the same with it. The priest must make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.
He must take the bull outside the camp and burn it as he burned the first bull. It is the congregation’s sin offering.
If a ruler sins unintentionally by doing any one of the things that the commandments of the Lord his God forbid, and becomes guilty,
if the sin he has committed becomes known to him, he must bring as his offering a young male goat without blemish.
he must lay his hand on the head of the male goat and slaughter it in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the Lord. It is a sin offering.

The priest must take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He must pour out its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.
He must offer up all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the burnt sacrifice. The priest must make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.
If any individual among the people of the land sins unintentionally by doing one of the things that the Lord’s commandments forbid, and becomes guilty,
If the sin he has committed becomes known to him, he shall bring as his offering a female goat without blemish for the sin he has committed.
He must lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter the sin offering in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and sprinkle it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He shall pour out all the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.

He shall remove all its fat, just as the fat is removed from the sacrifice of burnt offering. The priest shall burn it on the altar as an offering to the Lord, a pleasing aroma. The priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be forgiven.
If he brings his sin offering from the lambs, he shall bring a female without blemish.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter the sin offering in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and sprinkle it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He shall pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.

He shall deal with all its fat as he dealt with the fat of the lamb from the sacrifice of burnt offering. The priest shall burn these on the altar, on top of the Lord’s offerings. The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he shall be forgiven.
If a person sins by hearing a summons under oath when he is a witness, having seen or known something, but does not report it, he shall bear the guilt of his sin.

Or if a person touches anything unclean—the carcass of an unclean wild animal, the carcass of an unclean domestic animal, or the carcass of an unclean crawling creature—and fails to notice it, he has become unclean and has sinned.
Or if he touches human uncleanness, any uncleanness by which he may become unclean, and fails to notice it, but then realizes that he has sinned.

Or if a person swears, declaring with his lips that he will do harm or do good—anything that a person declares under oath—and fails to notice it, but then realizes that he has sinned in one of these matters.
When he has sinned in one of these things, he shall confess the sin he committed in that matter.
He shall bring his offering to the Lord for the sin he has committed: a female from the flock, a ewe lamb or a female goat, as a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for him for his sin.
If he cannot afford to bring a ewe lamb, he shall bring as the offering for his sin two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering.
He shall bring them to the priest, who shall offer the one for the sin offering first. He shall wring its head at the back of its neck but shall not detach it.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and the remaining blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
He shall prepare the other as a burnt offering according to its prescribed procedure. The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he shall be forgiven.

If he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall bring as his offering for the sin he has committed a tenth of a seah of fine flour as a sin offering. He shall not pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.
He shall bring it to the priest. The priest shall take a handful of it as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar, on top of the Lord’s offerings. It is a sin offering.
The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed in any one of these matters, and he shall be forgiven. The offering shall belong to the priest, as with the fine-flour offering.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:

If a person acts unfaithfully and unintentionally sins concerning the Lord’s holy things, he shall bring his offering to the Lord: a ram without blemish from the flock, valued in silver shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, as an offering.

He shall repay what he has wrongfully taken from the holy things and add a fifth of its value to it. He shall give it to the priest. The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the offering, and he shall be forgiven.
If a person sins and does any of the things forbidden by the Lord’s commandments, without knowing that he has sinned, he shall bear the guilt of his sin.

He shall bring to the priest a ram without blemish from the flock, of the required value, as an offering. The priest shall make atonement for him for the error he committed without knowing it, and he shall be forgiven.
It is an offering for sin; he shall bring an offering to the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:

If a person sins and acts unfaithfully against the Lord by deceiving his neighbor about something entrusted to him, or about a business partnership, or about something taken by force, or by defrauding his neighbor,
or if he finds something lost and lies about it, and swears falsely concerning any of these things that a person may do and thereby sin,
then, when he has sinned and become guilty, he shall return what he took by force, or what he obtained by fraud, or what was entrusted to him, or the lost property he found,
or anything about which he swore falsely. He shall repay its full value and add a fifth of its value to it. He shall give it to its owner on the day of his offering.
He must bring his offering to the LORD: a ram without defect from the flock, at the assessed value, as a guilt offering to the priest.
The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord, and he shall be forgiven for any of these things that a person does and thereby sins.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
Command Aaron and his sons and tell them: This is the law of the burnt offering. The burnt offering shall burn on the altar all night until morning, and the altar fire shall be kept burning on it.
The priest shall put on linen clothing and wear linen garments next to his body. He shall remove the ashes left when the fire consumes the burnt offering on the altar and place them beside the altar.
The priest shall take off his garments and put on other garments. He shall carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
The fire shall be kept burning on the altar and shall not go out. Every morning the priest shall pile wood on it, arrange the burnt offering on it, and burn the fat of the peace offerings on it.
The fire must be kept burning continually on the altar; it must not go out.
This is the law of the grain offering. Aaron’s sons must present it before the LORD, in front of the altar.

He shall take from it a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering and its oil, together with all the frankincense on the grain offering. He shall burn this on the altar as a pleasing aroma, a memorial portion for the Lord.
Aaron and his sons shall eat what remains of it. It shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place; they shall eat it in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it to them as their share of my offerings. It is most holy, like the sin offering and like the offering.
Every male among Aaron's descendants may eat it. This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations concerning the Lord's offerings. Whoever touches them shall become holy.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:

This is the offering of Aaron and his sons that they shall present to the Lord on the day he is anointed: a tenth of a seah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening, regularly.
It shall be prepared with oil on a griddle. He shall prepare it [?]. Break the grain offering into pieces and present it as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The priest from among his sons who is anointed to succeed him must prepare it. As a lasting ordinance, it must be burned completely to the LORD.
Every grain offering of a priest must be burned completely; it must not be eaten.”
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:

Speak to Aaron and his sons and tell them: This is the law of the sin offering. The sin offering shall be slaughtered before the Lord in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered. It is most holy.
The priest who offers it for purification must eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
Whoever touches its flesh shall become holy. If any of its blood splashes onto a garment, the garment on which it splashes shall be washed in a holy place.
The earthenware vessel in which it is cooked shall be broken. If it is cooked in a bronze vessel, the vessel shall be scoured and rinsed with water.
Every male among Aaron’s descendants may eat it, because it is most holy.
No sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the sanctuary shall be eaten. Instead, it shall be burned with fire.
This is the law of the guilt offering. It is most holy.
They shall slaughter the guilt offering in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, and they shall sprinkle its blood all around the altar.
He shall present all its fat from it: the fat tail and the fat covering the internal organs.
He shall prepare the two kidneys and their fat, and the lobe of the liver along with the kidneys.
The priest shall offer them up on the altar as an offering to the Lord. It is a sin offering.
Every male among Aaron's sons may eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.
The guilt offering is like the sin offering; you shall have one law for both. It shall belong to the priest who makes atonement with it.
When a priest presents a whole burnt offering for a man's sin, the hide of the whole burnt offering that he presents shall belong to the priest.
Every grain offering baked in an oven, and everything prepared in a pan or on a griddle, shall belong to the priest who presents it.
Every grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, shall belong to all Aaron's sons, each receiving his share.
This is the law of the sacrifice of the peace offering presented to the Lord.

If he presents it as a thanksgiving offering, he shall present with his thanksgiving sacrifice unleavened cakes mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and cakes of fine flour prepared [?] and mixed with oil.
Along with cakes of leavened bread, he shall present his offering with his thanksgiving sacrifice of peace offerings.
He shall present one of each of these offerings as a contribution to the Lord. It shall belong to the priest who sprinkles the blood of the burnt offering.
The flesh of the sacrifice of his thanksgiving burnt offering shall be eaten on the day he presents it. None of it shall be left until morning.
If the sacrifice he offers is for a vow or is a voluntary offering, it shall be eaten on the day the sacrifice is presented. Anything left over may also be eaten the next day.
Whatever remains of the meat of the sacrifice on the third day must be burned in the fire.

If any of the flesh of the burnt-offering sacrifice is eaten on the third day, it shall not be accepted or credited to the person who presents it. Instead, it shall be rejected, and anyone who eats it shall incur guilt.
Flesh that touches anything unclean shall not be eaten but shall be burned with fire. Anyone who is clean may eat the flesh.
Anyone who eats the flesh of the Lord's peace-offering sacrifice while unclean shall be destroyed from among their people.

If anyone touches any human uncleanness, or an unclean animal, or any unclean crawling creature, and eats meat from the sacrifice of the burnt offering belonging to the Lord, that person shall perish from among their people.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: You must not eat any fat from cattle, sheep, or goats.
The fat of an animal that has died and the fat of one eaten by wild animals may be used for any purpose, but you must not eat it.
For whoever eats fat from an animal from which an offering is presented to the Lord—that person who eats it shall perish from among their people.
You must not eat any blood, whether of birds or livestock, anywhere you live.
Anyone who eats blood shall be cut off from their people.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: Whoever presents a peace offering to the Lord shall bring his offering to the Lord from the sacrifice of the burnt offering.
His own hands shall bring the Lord’s offering. He shall bring the fat that is on the breast and wave what is set apart as an offering before the Lord.
The priest shall burn the fat on the altar, and the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons.
You shall give the right thigh as an offering set apart for the Lord from your peace offerings.
The right thigh shall belong as a portion to the one among Aaron’s sons who presents the blood and fat of the burnt offering.

For I have taken the breast set apart as an offering and the thigh set apart as an offering from the Israelites, from their peace offerings, and have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a perpetual due from the Israelites.
This is Aaron’s anointing portion and his sons’ anointing portion from the Lord’s offerings, on the day he is brought forward to serve the Lord.
The Lord commanded that these be given to them by the Israelites on the day he anointed them, as a perpetual due throughout their generations.
This is the law for the burning of the burnt offering, for the fine-flour offering, for the sin offering, for the offering, for the ordination offering, and for the sacrifice of the burnt offering.
The Lord commanded this to Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day he instructed him concerning the Israelites, that he should present their offerings to the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Bring Aaron and his sons with him, and take the garments, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
Gather the whole congregation at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Moses did as the Lord commanded him, and the whole congregation gathered before the tent of meeting.
Moses said to the whole congregation, “This is what the Lord has commanded to be done.”
Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
He clothed him in the tunic, fastened the sash around him, wrapped him in the robe, tied the apron around his waist, put the ephod on him, and secured it with the ephod’s waistband.
He placed the breastpiece over it and put Knowledge and Truth on the breastpiece.
He put the turban on his head and placed the gold crown, the holy crown, on the front of the turban, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, and consecrated them.
He sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times. He anointed the altar and all its utensils, and anointed the basin and its stand, consecrating them.
He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, anointed him, and consecrated him.
Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, clothed them in tunics, fastened sashes around them, and fitted them with caps, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He brought forward the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull for the sin offering.

He slaughtered it, and Moses took some of the blood with his finger and sprinkled it on the horns all around the altar, purifying the altar. He poured out the blood at the base of the altar and consecrated it, making atonement for it.
He took all the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and Moses offered them on the altar.
He burned the bull, its hide, its flesh, and its dung in the fire outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He brought forward the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
Moses slaughtered it and sprinkled some of its blood all around the altar.
He cut the ram into pieces, and Moses burned the heads, the pieces, and the fat.
He washed the entrails and the legs with water, and Moses offered the whole ram on the altar as a burnt offering, an offering to the Lord with a pleasing aroma, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He brought forward the second ram, the ram for ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
Moses slaughtered it, took some of its blood, and sprinkled it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

He brought Aaron’s sons forward, and Moses sprinkled some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Moses sprinkled the blood all around the altar.
He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.
From the basket of unleavened bread before the Lord, he took one unleavened cake [?], one cake [?] made with oil, and one flatbread, and placed them on the fat and on the right thigh.
He placed all of them in the hands of Aaron and his sons and set them apart as an offering before the Lord.
Moses took them from their hands and burned them on the altar as a burnt offering, to be an ordination offering with a pleasing aroma, an offering to the Lord.
Moses took the breast and set it apart as an offering before the Lord. It was Moses’ share of the ram of ordination, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood on the altar and sprinkled it on Aaron and his clothes, and on his sons and their clothes with him. He consecrated Aaron and his clothes, and his sons and their clothes with him.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons, “Boil the meat at the entrance of the tent of meeting. Eat it there with the bread in the basket of ordination, as I was commanded: ‘Aaron and his sons shall eat it.’”
Whatever remains of the meat and the bread you shall burn in the fire.
“Do not leave the entrance of the tent of meeting for seven days, until the days of your ordination are completed, because your ordination takes seven days.”
The Lord commanded that what I have done today be done to make atonement for you.
“Stay at the entrance of the tent of meeting day and night for seven days, and keep the Lord’s requirements so that you do not die, for this is what I was commanded.”
Aaron and his sons did everything the Lord had commanded through Moses.
On the eighth day, Moses called Aaron, his sons, and the elders of the Israelites.
He said to Aaron, “Take a young bull calf for yourself as a sin offering and a ram without blemish as a whole burnt offering, and present them before the Lord.”
“Tell the Israelites, ‘Take a male goat as a sin offering, and a calf and lambs a year old, without blemish, as a burnt offering.’”
“‘Also take an ox and a ram as a peace offering before the Lord, and fine flour mixed with oil, because today the Lord will appear to you.’”
They took everything Moses had commanded them and came before the tent of meeting. The entire congregation approached and stood before the Lord.
Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.”

Moses said to Aaron, “Approach the altar and offer your sin offering and your whole burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people. Then present the people’s offering and make atonement for them, as the Lord commanded.”
Aaron approached the altar and slaughtered the calf for his own sin offering.
Aaron’s sons brought him the blood. He dipped his finger in the blood and sprinkled it on the horns of the altar, and he poured out the blood at the base of the altar.
He offered the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering on the altar, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He burned the meat and the hide in the fire outside the camp.
He slaughtered the whole burnt offering. Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he sprinkled it all around the altar.
They handed him the whole burnt offering. He cut it up limb by limb and offered the head on the altar.
He washed the entrails and the legs and offered the whole burnt offering on the altar.
He presented the people's offering. He took the male goat for the people's sin offering, slaughtered it, and offered it for purification like the first one.
He presented the whole burnt offering and offered it according to its prescribed procedure.
He presented the fine flour, took a handful of it, and offered it on the altar in addition to the morning whole burnt offering.
He slaughtered the ox and the ram as the people’s peace offering. Aaron’s sons handed him the blood, and he sprinkled it all around the altar.
And the fat from the bull and the ram, the fat tail, the membrane covering the entrails, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver.
He placed the fat on the breasts and offered the fat on the altar.
Aaron set apart the breasts and the right thigh as a special offering before the LORD, as Moses had been commanded.
Aaron raised his hands over the people and blessed them. Then he came down after offering the sin offering, the whole burnt offering, and the peace offering.
Moses and Aaron entered the tent of meeting. They came out and blessed the people, and the glory of the Lord appeared before all the people.
Fire came out from before the Lord and consumed the fat and the whole burnt offering on the altar. All the people saw it and offered praise, and they fell facedown.

Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu each took his censer, put fire in it, and placed incense on it. They offered unauthorized fire before the Lord at an improper time, which he had not commanded them to offer.
Fire came out from before the Lord and consumed them, and they died before the Lord.
Moses said to Aaron, “This is what the Lord said: ‘Among those who draw near to me I will be shown holy, and before all the people I will be glorified.’” Aaron remained silent.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Aaron’s uncle Uzziel, and said to them, “Come forward and carry your brothers away from the front of the sanctuary to outside the camp.”
They came forward, picked them up in their tunics, and carried them outside the camp, as Moses had said.

Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his surviving sons, “Do not uncover your heads or tear your clothes, so that you do not die and wrath does not come upon the entire congregation. But let all your fellow Israelites mourn those whom the Lord burned.”
“Do not leave the entrance of the tent of meeting, so that you do not die, because the Lord’s anointing oil is upon you.” They did as Moses said.
The LORD said to Aaron:
“You and your sons with you must not drink wine or strong drink when you enter the tent of meeting, so that you do not die. This is a lasting statute throughout your generations.”
so that you may distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the unclean and the clean.
You shall teach the Israelites all the statutes that the Lord spoke to them through Moses.
Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his surviving sons, “Take the fine flour left over from the Lord’s offerings and eat it unleavened beside the altar, because it is most holy.”
Eat it in a holy place, because it is your allotted portion and the allotted portion of your sons with you from the offerings of the Lord, for so I have been commanded.

Eat the breast set apart and the thigh set apart in a clean place, you and your sons and daughters with you, because they have been given as your allotted portion and the allotted portion of your sons with you from the peace offerings of the Israelites.

They shall bring the thigh set apart and the breast set apart along with the offering of fat, to set them apart as an offering before the Lord. They shall be a perpetual allotted portion for you and your sons with you, as the Lord commanded.
Moses searched diligently for the goat of the sin offering, and it had been burned. He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s remaining sons, and said to them:
“Why did you not eat the sin offering in a holy place? It is most holy, and I gave it to you to take away the congregation’s sin and make atonement for them before the Lord.
Look, none of its blood was brought into the inner sanctuary. You should have eaten it in the sanctuary, as I was commanded: Aaron and his sons shall eat it.”

Aaron said to Moses, “Look, today they offered their sin offerings and their whole burnt offerings before the Lord, and all these things have happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would that have been pleasing to the Lord?”
Moses heard this, and it was pleasing in his eyes.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: “These are the living creatures you may eat from among all the animals on the earth.
You may eat any animal whose hoof is split and divided in two and that chews the cud.
But these you shall not eat among those that chew the cud or have split hooves: the camel, because it chews the cud but does not have split hooves, is unclean for you.
the hyrax, which chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, is unclean for you;
the hare, which chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, is unclean for you;
and the pig, whose hoof is split and divided in two but which does not chew the cud, is unclean for you.
You shall not eat their meat or approach their carcasses. They are unclean for you.
These you may eat from among everything in the water: eat whatever has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas and in the streams.
Whatever does not have fins and scales in the seas and streams, among all the creatures that swarm in the water and all the living creatures in the water, is unclean for you.
You shall not eat their meat, and you shall regard their carcasses as unclean.
Anything in the water that does not have fins and scales is unclean for you.
And these you must detest among the birds; they must not be eaten, because they are unclean: the eagle,
and the kite,
and ravens of their various kinds,
and ostriches and hawks of their various kinds,
and the little owl, the fish hawk, and the owl,
and the swan, the pelican, and the bee-eater,
and the stork and herons of their various kinds, and the wild rooster and the peacock.
And all winged insects that walk on all fours are unclean for you.
These you may eat from among all the winged creatures that walk on all fours: those that have claws above their feet with which to leap on the ground.
These you may eat among them: locusts of their various kinds and grasshoppers of their various kinds.
And every winged insect that has four feet is unclean for you.
And by these you will become unclean: anyone who touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening.
And anyone who carries their carcasses must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening.
Every animal whose hoof is split but not divided in two, and that does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. Whoever touches them shall be unclean until evening.
Whatever walks on its paws among all the creatures that walk on all fours is unclean for you. Whoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
Whoever carries their carcasses shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening, because they are unclean for you.
These are unclean among all the creatures that crawl on the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the lizard, according to their kinds.
and the [?], the mole, the lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
These are unclean among all the crawling creatures. Anyone who touches them when they are dead will be unclean until evening.

Anything on which one of them falls when dead shall become unclean. Any wooden utensil, garment, hide, sackcloth, or any implement used for work shall be immersed in water. They shall be unclean until evening, and then they shall be clean.
And any earthenware vessel into which one of them falls—everything inside it will be unclean, and you must break the vessel.
Any food that is eaten shall become unclean if water falls on it, and any drink that is drunk in any vessel shall become unclean.
Anything on which any part of their carcasses falls shall be unclean. An oven or a cooking hearth shall be torn down. They are unclean and shall remain unclean for you.
However, springs, cisterns, and collections of water shall remain clean, but whoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean.
And if any part of their carcasses falls on any seed intended for sowing, it remains clean.
If water falls on seed and any of their carcasses falls on it, it is unclean for you.
If an animal that is clean for you to eat dies, whoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone who carries its carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening.
Every crawling creature that crawls on the earth is unclean for you. You shall not eat it.
You shall not eat any creature that crawls on its belly, walks on all fours, or has many feet, among all the creatures that crawl on the earth, because they are unclean.
Do not make yourselves unclean through any creature that crawls on the earth, so that you do not become unclean through them. Do not become unclean through them.
For I am the Lord your God. Consecrate yourselves and be holy, because I am holy. Do not make yourselves unclean through any creature that crawls on the earth.
For I am the Lord your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God. You shall be holy, because I am holy.”
This is the law concerning animals and birds, every living creature that moves in the water, and every creature that moves on the earth.
