The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When a woman conceives and gives birth to a boy, she shall be unclean for seven days. She shall be unclean as she is during the days of her menstrual period.
On the eighth day they shall circumcise the flesh of his foreskin.
She shall remain in the period of blood purification for thirty-three days. She shall not approach anything holy or enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.
If she gives birth to a girl, she shall be unclean for fourteen days, as during her menstrual period. She shall remain in the period of blood purification for sixty-six days.

When the days of her purification for a son or a daughter are completed, she shall bring a year-old lamb as a whole burnt offering and a turtledove or a young pigeon as a sin offering to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
He shall present it before the Lord and make atonement for her, and she shall be cleansed from the flow of her blood. This is the law for a woman who gives birth to a boy or a girl.

If she cannot afford to bring a lamb, she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one as a sin offering and one as a whole burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:

When a person has a swelling, a scab, or a bright spot on the skin of his body, and it becomes a swelling from a leprous lesion on the skin of his body, he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who are priests.

The priest shall [?] the lesion on the skin of his body. If the lesion has spread on the skin of his body, the hair in the lesion has turned white, and the lesion appears deeper than the skin of his body, it is a leprous lesion. The priest shall examine it and declare him unclean.
If the bright spot on the skin of his body is white and does not appear deeper than the skin [?], and the hair has not turned white, the priest shall isolate the affected person for seven days.
The priest shall examine it on the seventh day. If the lesion has remained in the same place and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall isolate him for another seven days.

The priest shall examine it after another seven days. If the lesion has faded and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall declare him clean, because it is a rash. He shall wash his clothes and be clean.
But if the bright spot spreads further on the skin after the priest has examined it and declared him clean, it shall be shown to the priest again.
The priest shall examine it. If the bright spot has spread on the skin, the priest shall declare the person unclean, because it is leprosy.
When someone has a leprous lesion, he shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall examine it. If there is a white swelling on the skin, it has turned the hair white, and there is a patch of raw flesh in the swelling,
it is chronic leprosy on the skin of his body. The priest shall declare him unclean and shall not isolate him, because he is unclean.
If the leprosy breaks out over his skin and covers all his skin, from his head to his feet, everywhere the priest can see,
the priest shall examine him. If the leprosy has covered his whole body, he shall declare the lesion clean, for it has all turned white; he is clean.
But whenever raw flesh appears on him, he shall be unclean.
The priest shall examine the raw flesh and declare the raw flesh unclean. It is unclean because it is leprosy.
But if the raw flesh turns white again, he shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall examine it. If the lesion has turned white, the priest shall declare the lesion clean, because it is clean.
If a boil develops on a person's skin and heals,
If a white swelling or a white or red bright spot appears where the boil was, it shall be shown to the priest.
The priest shall examine it. If it appears lower than the skin and its hair has turned white, the priest shall declare him unclean, because it is a leprous lesion that has developed in the boil.
But if the priest sees that there is no white hair in it and that it is not lower than the skin but is level with it, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
If it spreads in the skin, the priest shall declare it unclean, because it is a lesion of leprosy.
But if the bright spot remains in its place and does not spread, it is the scar of the boil. The priest shall declare it clean.
If a person has a burn from fire on the skin of his body, and a white, red, or whitish bright spot appears in the swelling of the burn,

the priest shall examine it. If the hair in the bright spot has turned white and it appears deeper than the skin, it is leprosy that has broken out in the burn. The priest shall declare him unclean, because it is a leprous lesion.
But if the priest sees that there is no white hair in the bright spot and that it is not lower than the skin but is level with it, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day. If the bright spot has spread on the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean, because it is a leprous lesion.
But if the bright spot stays in the same place and has not spread over the skin, but has faded, it is a scar from the burn. The priest shall declare it clean, because it is a scar from the burn.
If a man or woman has a lesion on the head or beard,

The priest shall examine the affected area. If it appears deeper than the skin and has thin yellow hair in it, the priest shall declare it unclean, because it is an outbreak of leprosy on the head or beard.
But if the priest examines the affected area and it does not appear deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, the priest shall isolate the affected area for seven days.
The priest shall examine that affected area on the seventh day. If it has not spread, if there is no yellow hair in it, and if it does not appear deeper than the skin,
he shall shave around the affected area but shall not shave the area itself. The priest shall isolate the affected area for another seven days.

The priest shall examine the affected area on the seventh day. If it has not spread over the skin and does not appear deeper than the skin, the priest shall declare it clean. The person shall wash his clothes and be clean.
But if the lesion spreads in the skin after he has been declared clean,
The priest shall examine it. If the affected area has spread over the skin, the priest shall not inquire about yellow hair, because the person is unclean.
But if the affected area stays in the same place and black hair has grown in it, the affected area is healing, because it is clean. The priest shall declare it clean.
If a man or a woman has a bright, white spot on the skin of their body,
The priest shall examine them. If there is a white or reddish bright spot on the skin of their bodies, it is a scaly eruption that has spread over the skin; the person is clean.
If a man's hair falls out and he becomes bald, he is clean.
If his hair falls out at the front of his head, he is bald at the forehead; he is clean.
If there is a white or reddish affected area on the bald back or front of his head, it is leprosy that has spread on the bald back or front of his head.
The priest shall examine the swelling of the affected area. If it is white or reddish on the bald back or front of his head, it has the appearance of leprosy on the skin of his body.
That man has leprosy and is unclean. The priest shall declare him unclean because the lesion is on his head.
Anyone who has leprosy and has an affected area shall wear torn clothes, leave his head uncovered, cover his lips, and call himself unclean.
As long as he has the affected area, he shall remain unclean. Because he is unclean, he shall live alone, and his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
If a garment has a leprous lesion, whether it is a woolen garment or a linen garment,
or in the warp or the weft of linen or wool, or in leather or anything made of leather,
If the affected area is greenish or reddish on a garment or a hide, on the warp or the weft, or on any leather article, it is an outbreak of leprosy. They shall show it to the priest.
The priest shall examine the affected spot, and the priest shall isolate it for seven days.

The priest shall examine the affected area on the seventh day. If it has spread in the garment, the warp or the weft, the hide, or any leather made into an article for use, it is an outbreak of malignant leprosy. It is unclean.
He shall burn the garment, the warp or the weft of wool or linen, or any leather article that has the affected area. He shall burn it in fire, because it is malignant leprosy.
But if the priest sees that the affected area has not spread in the garment, the warp or the weft, or any leather article,
the priest shall order them to wash the thing that has the affected area, and the priest shall isolate it for another seven days.

The priest shall examine the affected area after they have washed it. But the appearance of the affected area has changed, and the affected area has not changed or spread. It is unclean. Burn it in fire. It is an affected area in either its new or its worn part.
But if the priest sees that the affected area has faded after it was washed, he shall tear it out and remove it from the garment, the hide, the warp, or the weft.
If it appears again in the garment, the warp or the weft, or any leather article, they shall burn it in fire, because the affected area has spread in it.
A garment, warp or weft, or any leather article that has been washed and from which the affected area has disappeared shall be washed a second time and be clean.
This is the law concerning an outbreak of leprosy in a woolen or linen garment, in the warp or the weft, or in any leather article, for declaring it clean or unclean.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
This shall be the law concerning a person with leprosy on the day he is cleansed: he shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall go outside the camp, and the priest shall examine whether the man's leprous lesion has healed.
The priest shall order them to bring, for the person being cleansed, two live, clean birds, cedarwood, scarlet-dyed material, and hyssop.
The priest shall order them to slaughter one bird in an earthenware vessel over spring water.

He shall take the other, living bird, the cedarwood, the scarlet-dyed material, and the hyssop, and dip them, together with the living bird, in the blood of the bird that was slaughtered over spring water.
He must sprinkle the person being cleansed from leprosy seven times, and he will be clean. He must release the living bird into the open fields.
The person being cleansed must wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and bathe in water, and he will be clean. Afterward he may enter the camp, but he must stay outside his tent for seven days.
On the seventh day he must shave off all his hair—his head, his beard, and his eyebrows. He must shave off all his hair, wash his clothes, and bathe his body in water, and he will be clean.
On the eighth day he must take two male lambs without blemish, one year-old ewe lamb without blemish, three tenths of a measure of fine, sifted flour mixed with oil, and a flask of oil.
The priest who performs the cleansing must present the man being cleansed, together with these things, before the Lord at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest must take one lamb and offer it as a sin offering, together with the flask of oil. The priest must set them apart as an offering before the Lord.
He must slaughter the lamb in the holy place where the sin offering and the whole burnt offering are slaughtered, because the offering for sin belongs to the priest; it is most holy.
The priest must take some of the blood of the sin offering and sprinkle it on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on his right thumb, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall take one measure of oil and pour it into the priest’s left hand.
The priest must dip his right finger into the oil in his left hand, and with his finger the priest must sprinkle some of the oil seven times before the Lord.

From the oil remaining in his hand, the priest must sprinkle some on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on his right thumb, and on the big toe of his right foot, where the blood of the sin offering was placed.
He must put the oil left in the priest’s hand on the head of the person being cleansed, and the priest must make atonement for him before the Lord.
The priest must present the sin offering and make atonement for the person being cleansed from his uncleanness. Afterward he must slaughter the whole burnt offering.
The priest must offer up the whole burnt offering and the fine flour on the altar. The priest must make atonement for him, and he will be clean.

If he is poor and cannot afford these things, he must take one lamb as a sin offering to be set apart, to make atonement for him, one tenth of a seah of sifted flour mixed with oil as an offering, and one flask of oil.
He must also take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford. One must be a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.
On the eighth day he must bring them to the priest for his cleansing, to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting before the Lord.
The priest must take one lamb and the log-measure of oil, and the priest must set them apart as a dedicated offering before the Lord.

He must slaughter the lamb for the sin offering. The priest must take some of the blood of the sin offering and sprinkle it on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on his right thumb, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest must pour some of the oil into his own left hand.
With his right finger, the priest must sprinkle some of the oil in his left hand seven times before the Lord.

The priest must sprinkle some of the oil in his hand on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on his right thumb, and on the big toe of his right foot, where the blood of the sin offering was placed.
He must sprinkle the oil left in the priest’s hand on the head of the person being cleansed and make atonement for him before the Lord.
He must offer some of the turtledoves or young pigeons, whichever he can afford.
One must be a sin offering and the other a burnt offering, together with the fine flour. The priest must make atonement before the Lord for the person being cleansed.
This is the law for someone who has an affliction of leprosy and cannot afford what is required for his cleansing.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as an inheritance, and I put an outbreak of leprosy in a house in the land you possess,
the owner of the house must come and report to the priest, saying to him, “Something like an outbreak of leprosy has appeared to me in the house.”
The priest must order the house to be emptied before he enters to examine the outbreak, so that everything in the house does not become unclean. Afterward the priest must enter.
He must examine the outbreak. If the outbreak on the wall of the house consists of greenish or reddish patches that appear deeper than the wall,
the priest shall leave the house, stand at its doorway, and shut up that house for seven days.
The priest shall return on the seventh day and see whether the affected area has spread on the wall of the house.
the priest must order them to pull out the stones affected by the outbreak of leprosy and throw them outside the town in an unclean place.
They must scrape the inside of that house all around and throw the dust they have scraped off outside the town in an unclean place.
They shall take other stones and put them in place of the stones, and they shall take fresh plaster and plaster the house.
If the disease spreads and increases in the house after the stones have been removed and after the house has been scraped and replastered,
the priest shall enter and inspect it. If the disease has spread in the house, there is a malignant leprous disease in the house; it is unclean.
They shall tear down the house—its stones, its timbers, and all its plaster—and carry it outside the town to an unclean place and burn it with fire.
Anyone who enters the house during any of the days when it is shut up shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone who sleeps inside the house shall wash his clothes, and anyone who eats inside the house shall wash his clothes.
If the priest enters and sees that the disease has not spread in the house after the house was plastered, the priest shall declare that house clean, because the disease has healed.
For the purification of the house, he shall take two living, clean birds, cedarwood, hyssop, and scarlet-dyed material. And the priest shall give orders.
and they shall slaughter one bird in an earthenware vessel over spring water.

He shall take the other bird, the living one, along with the cedarwood, hyssop, and scarlet-dyed material, and dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in fresh running water. He shall sprinkle that house seven times.
He shall purify the house with the bird’s blood, the fresh running water, the living bird, the cedarwood, the hyssop, and the scarlet-dyed material.
He shall release the living bird outside the town into the open country. He shall make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.
This shall be the law for every leprous affliction and for an affected area,
for leprous disease in clothing or in a house,
and for a swelling, a scab, or a bright spot,
and for distinguishing between the unclean and the clean. This is the law concerning leprous disease.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them,
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When any man has a discharge from his body, his discharge is unclean.
This shall be the uncleanness of his discharge: whether his body flows with the discharge or his body is blocked from discharging, it is his uncleanness.
Every bed on which the man with the discharge lies shall be unclean, and every article on which he sits shall be unclean.
Anyone who touches his bed shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone who sits on an article on which the man with the discharge has sat shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches the body of the man with the discharge shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.
If the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.
Anything on which the man with a discharge rides will be unclean.
Anyone who touches anything that is beneath him shall be unclean until evening. Anyone who carries those things shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches the man with the discharge, when he has not washed his hands in water, shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.
An earthenware vessel touched by the man with the discharge shall be broken, and every wooden or bronze vessel shall be rinsed with water.

When the man with the discharge becomes clean from his discharge, he shall count off seven days for himself and be purified. He shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in fresh running water, and he shall be clean.
On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them before the Lord to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and give them to the priest.
The priest shall offer them, one as a sin offering and the other as a whole burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord for his discharge.
If a man has an emission of semen, he shall bathe his whole body in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.
Any cloth or bed on which semen falls shall be washed with water, and it shall be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, they shall bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
When a woman has a discharge of blood, her discharge being in her body, she shall remain in her menstrual impurity for seven days. Anyone who touches her shall be unclean until evening.
Anything on which she lies during her menstrual impurity will be unclean, and anything on which she sits will be unclean.
Anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches any article she sits on shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.
If someone touches the bedding or the object on which she sits, he will be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with her and her menstrual impurity comes upon him, he shall be unclean for seven days. Every bed he lies on shall be unclean.

If a woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside the time of her menstrual period, or if her discharge continues beyond her menstrual period, all the days when she has this unclean discharge shall be like the days of her menstrual period, and she shall be unclean.

Every bed she lies on throughout the days of her discharge shall be for her like the bed of her menstrual period. Every article she sits on shall be unclean, as with the uncleanness of her menstrual period.
Anyone who touches them shall become unclean. He shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.
When she becomes free of her discharge, she must count off seven days for herself, and afterward she will be clean.
On the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest shall offer them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for her before the Lord for her unclean discharge.
You shall warn the Israelites about their uncleanness, so that they do not die in their uncleanness and do not defile my tabernacle that is among them.
This shall be the law for anyone who has a discharge, and for anyone who emits semen during intercourse and becomes unclean through it,

The menstruating woman shall be in her menstrual impurity, and whoever has a discharge shall be in the condition of that discharge, whether male or female, as shall a man who lies with an unclean woman.
The Lord spoke with Moses after Aaron's two sons died, when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord and died.

The Lord said to Moses, "Speak to Aaron your brother, so that he does not enter the sanctuary at just any time, inside the curtain in front of the atonement cover on the ark, lest he die. For I appear in the cloud above the atonement cover.
This is how Aaron shall enter the sanctuary: with a young bull as a sin offering and a ram as a whole burnt offering.

He shall put on a holy linen tunic, and linen undergarments shall cover his body. He shall fasten a linen sash around himself and put a linen turban on his head, for these are holy garments. He shall bathe his body in water and put them on.
From the congregation of the Israelites he shall take two male goats as a sin offering and one ram as a burnt offering.
Aaron shall offer his own bull as a sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household.
He shall take the two male goats and present them alive before the Lord at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Aaron shall cast lots over the two goats, one lot for the Lord and one lot for Azazel.
Aaron shall bring forward the male goat on which the Lord’s lot fell and offer it as a sin offering.
The goat on which the lot for Azazel falls shall be presented alive before the Lord, so that atonement may be made over it, and it shall be sent away to Azazel in the wilderness.
Aaron shall bring forward the bull for his own sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household. He shall slaughter the bull of the sin offering.
He shall take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the Lord, and two handfuls of incense made from fragrant spices, and bring them inside the curtain.
He shall put the incense on the fire before the Lord, so that the cloud of incense covers the atonement cover that is over the testimony, and he does not die.

He shall take some of the bull's blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the atonement cover, on its eastern side. Before the atonement cover he shall sprinkle some of the blood seven times with his finger.

He shall slaughter the goat that is the people's sin offering and bring its blood inside the curtain. He shall do with its blood as he did with the bull's blood, sprinkling it on the atonement cover and before the atonement cover.

He shall make atonement for the sanctuary because of the uncleanness of the Israelites, their wrongdoing, and all their sins. He shall do the same for the tent of meeting, which stands with them amid their uncleanness.

No one shall be in the tent of meeting from the time he enters to make atonement in the sanctuary until he comes out. He shall make atonement for himself and his household, and he shall make atonement for the whole congregation of the Israelites.

He shall go out to the altar that is before the Lord and make atonement for it. He shall take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood and sprinkle it on the horns of the altar all around.
He must sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, cleansing it and making it holy from the uncleanness of the Israelites.
When he has finished making atonement for the holy places, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he shall bring forward the living male goat.

Aaron must lay both his hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the wrongdoing of the Israelites, all their wickedness and all their sins. He must place them on the goat’s head and send it into the wilderness with a man who is ready for the task.
The male goat shall carry all their wrongdoing upon itself to a desolate land, and the man shall release the male goat in the wilderness.
Aaron must enter the tent of meeting, take off the linen garments he wore when he entered the sanctuary, and leave them there.

He must bathe his body in water in a holy place, put on his clothes, and come out. He must offer his whole burnt offering and the people’s whole burnt offering, and make atonement for himself and for the people.
He shall offer the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
The man who sends the goat away to Azazel must wash his clothes and bathe in water. Afterward he may enter the camp.

They must take outside the camp the bull for the sin offering and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the sanctuary to make atonement. They must burn their hides, their flesh, and their dung in the fire.
The man who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Then he may enter the camp.
This must be a lasting law for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you must humble yourselves and do no work, neither you nor those who turn to me and live among you.
For on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you from all your sins. You will be clean before the Lord.
It is a Sabbath of rest for you, and you must humble yourselves. This is a lasting law.
The priest who is anointed and ordained to serve in his father’s place must make atonement. He must put on the linen garments and the holy vestments.
He must make atonement for the Most Holy Place, the tent of meeting, and the altar. He must also make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
This must be a lasting law for you: atonement must be made for the Israelites for all their sins once a year. And they did as the Lord commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites, and tell them: This is what the Lord has commanded:
Any man among the Israelites who slaughters an ox, a lamb, or a goat in the camp, or who slaughters it outside the camp,

and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it as an offering to the Lord before the Lord’s tabernacle—that man will be held guilty of bloodshed, because he has shed blood. That man must be cut off from among his people.

This is so that the Israelites will bring the sacrifices they slaughter in the open fields, bringing them before the Lord to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and slaughtering them as peace offerings to the Lord.
The priest must sprinkle the blood on the Lord’s altar at the entrance of the tent of meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
They must no longer offer their sacrifices to the demons they stray after. This must be a lasting law for them throughout their generations.
And tell them: Any man of the house of Israel, or of those who turn to me and live among you, who offers a whole burnt offering or a sacrifice
and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it before the Lord—that man must be cut off from among his people.
Any man of Israel, or of those who turn to me and live in Israel, who eats blood—I will direct my anger against the person who eats blood and cut that person off from among their people.
For the life of the flesh is the blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives, because it is the blood that makes atonement for a life.
That is why I told the Israelites: No one among you may eat blood, and those who turn to me and live with you must not eat blood.
Any man among the Israelites, or among those who turn to me and live among you, who hunts and catches an animal or a bird that may be eaten must pour out its blood and cover it with dust.
For the life of all flesh is the blood. And tell the Israelites: You must not eat the blood of any flesh, because the life of all flesh is the blood. Anyone who eats it must be cut off.

Anyone who eats an animal found dead or torn by a wild beast, whether one of you or one of those who turn to me and live among you, must wash their clothes and bathe in water. They will be unclean until evening, and then they will be clean.
But if he does not wash his clothes or bathe his body, he must bear the guilt of his sin.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: I am the Lord your God.
Do not follow the practices of the land of Egypt, where you lived. Do not follow the practices of the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you, and do not live by their laws.
Instead, carry out my judgments, keep my commandments, and live by them. I am the Lord your God.
Keep my commandments and my judgments. The person who carries them out will live by them. I am the Lord.
None of you must approach any close blood relative to uncover their nakedness. I am the Lord.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your father or the nakedness of your mother. She is your mother; you must not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife, for it is your father’s nakedness.
Do not uncover the nakedness of your sister, your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, whether she was born to your father or to another man. Do not uncover her nakedness.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, for their nakedness is your own nakedness.
The daughter of your father's wife, born to your father, is your sister. You must not uncover her nakedness.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister, for she is your father's close relative.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, because she is your mother's close relative.
Do not uncover the nakedness of your uncle's wife. Do not approach his wife, because she is your uncle's wife. Do not uncover her nakedness.
You must not uncover your daughter-in-law's nakedness. Because she is your son's wife, you must not uncover her nakedness.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife, for it is your brother's nakedness.
Do not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. Do not approach her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to uncover their nakedness. They are close relatives, and this is wickedness.
You must not marry a woman in addition to her sister, causing her distress and uncovering the other woman's nakedness alongside her during her lifetime.
You must not approach a woman to uncover her nakedness during her menstrual uncleanness.
You must not deposit your semen in your neighbor's wife through intercourse and defile yourself with her.
You must not deposit any of your semen to make a foreign woman pregnant, and you must not profane the name of your God. I am the Lord.
You must not lie with a male as one lies with a woman, because it is unclean.
Do not deposit your semen in any animal and defile yourself with it. A woman must not stand before an animal to be mounted by it, because this is uncleanness.
Do not defile yourselves with any of these things, because the nations I am driving out before you defiled themselves with all these things.
The land became defiled, and I punished it for its wrongdoing, and the land cast out its inhabitants.
Keep my statutes and judgments. Do not commit any of these sins, neither you nor those who turn to me and live among you.
For the people of the land who were there before you committed all these sins, and the land became defiled.
Do not defile the land, so that it does not cast you out as it cast out the nation that was there before you.
For whoever commits any of these sins—the people who do them will perish from among their people.
Keep my requirements, and do not follow the sinful customs practiced by those before you. Do not defile yourselves with them. I am the Lord your God.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
Speak to the whole assembly of the Israelites and tell them: Be holy, because I am holy. I am the Lord your God.
Each of you must fear his father and his mother. Keep my commandments, because I am the Lord your God.
Do not turn to demons, and do not make gods of cast metal for yourselves. I am the Lord your God.
When you offer sacrifices of well-being to the Lord, offer them so that they will be accepted.
They are to be eaten on the day they are sacrificed, and they may be eaten the next day. Whatever remains until the third day must be burned in fire and must not be eaten.
If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is detestable and will not be accepted.
Anyone who eats any of it will bear guilt, because they have defiled what is holy to the Lord. That person will perish from among their people.
When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap the edges of your fields completely, and do not gather the gleanings of your harvest.
Do not strip your vineyards bare, and do not gather the fallen olives from your olive trees. Instead, leave them for the poor and for those who turn to me, because I am the Lord your God.
Do not steal. Do not lie. Do not deceive one another.
Do not swear falsely by my name and so profane the name of your God. I am the Lord.
Do not wrong your neighbor or treat him with violence. Do not keep a hired worker's wages with you overnight until morning.
Do not insult a deaf person or put a stumbling block before a blind person. Instead, fear your God. I am the Lord.
Do not act unjustly in judgment. Do not favor the poor or show partiality to the powerful. Instead, judge your neighbor fairly.
You shall not slander your people, and you shall not act against your neighbor’s life, for I am the Lord.
Do not hate your brother in your heart. Instead, firmly rebuke your neighbor, so that you do not bear sin because of him.
Do not harbor hostility toward the members of your people. Instead, love your neighbor as yourself. I am the Lord.
Keep my commandments. Do not crossbreed your livestock. Do not sow your fields with mixed seed. Do not wear garments woven from mixed materials.

If a man has sexual intercourse with a woman who is a slave purchased for a man, and she has not been redeemed or given her freedom, they must be subjected to an inquiry, but they must not be put to death, because she had not been freed.
He shall bring his offering to the Lord, to the entrance of the tent of meeting: a ram as a sin offering.
The priest must make atonement for him before the Lord with the ram of the sin offering, for the sin he committed. Then the sin he committed will be forgiven him.
When you enter the land and plant any trees for food, leave them alone for three years and do not eat their fruit.
In the fourth year, all their fruit shall be holy, an offering of praise to the Lord.
In the fifth year, eat their fruit, and they will increase their yield for you. I am the Lord your God.
Do not eat blood. Do not look for omens in birds. Do not practice divination.
Do not let the hair of your heads grow long, and do not disfigure the edges of your beards.
Do not make cuts in your flesh for a dead person, and do not make tattooed markings on yourselves. I am the Lord.
Do not allow your daughter to prostitute herself, so that the land does not become a prostitute and become filled with sin.
Instead, keep my commandments and revere my sanctuary. I am the Lord.
Do not turn to mediums or spiritists, and do not consult them, so that you do not become unclean through them. I am the Lord your God.
Stand up in the presence of an elderly person, honor anyone older than you, and fear your God. I am the Lord.
When someone who turns to me lives among you, do not mistreat him.
Rather, he shall be like you and one of you. Love those who turn to me and live among you as yourselves, because you too were foreigners living in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
Do not act unjustly in judgment, in the scales, in weights, or in measures.
You must have honest scales, honest weights, an honest dry measure, and an honest liquid measure. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
Keep all my commandments and all my laws, and carry them out. I am the Lord.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:

Tell the Israelites: Any man among the Israelites or among those who turn to me and live in Israel who deposits his seed in a foreign woman must certainly be put to death. The people of the land must stone that man.
I will direct my anger against that man and destroy him from among his people, because he deposited his seed in a foreign woman, defiling my sanctuary and defiling my holy name.
If the people of the land avert their eyes from that man who deposited his seed in a foreign woman, so as not to put him to death,
I will bring my anger against that man and his family. I will destroy him and all who go astray after him from among their people, because they go astray after foreign women.
If anyone turns to mediums and spiritists and goes astray after them, I will direct my anger against that person and destroy that person from among their people.
Consecrate yourselves and be holy, because I am the Lord your God.
Keep my commandments and carry them out. I am the Lord who makes you holy.
A man who curses his father or his mother must be put to death. He has cursed his father or his mother; his blood is on his own head.
If a man commits adultery with another man's wife, committing adultery with his neighbor's wife, both the adulterer and the adulteress must certainly be put to death.
If a man sleeps with his father's wife, he has exposed his father's nakedness. Both of them must certainly be put to death. Their blood is on their own heads.
If a man sleeps with his daughter-in-law, both of them must certainly be put to death. Because they have committed a sin, their blood is on their own heads.
If a man sleeps with a male as one sleeps with a woman, they have committed a detestable act. Both of them must certainly be put to death. Their blood is on their own heads.
If a man marries a woman and her mother, it is a sin. They must burn him and the women with fire, so that there may be no sin among you.
If a man sleeps with an animal, he shall certainly be put to death, and the animal shall also be stoned.
If a woman approaches an animal to be mounted by it, kill the woman and the animals as well. They must certainly be put to death. Their blood is on their own heads.

If a man marries his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness, and she also sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace. They must be destroyed in the sight of their own people. He has exposed his sister's nakedness; they must bear their guilt.
If a man sleeps with a menstruating woman and exposes her nakedness, he has exposed her flow, and she has exposed the flow of her blood. Both of them must be destroyed from among their people.
Do not expose the nakedness of your mother's sister or your father's sister, because they are close relatives. Nakedness [?]. They must bear their guilt.
If a man sleeps with his uncle's wife, he has exposed his uncle's nakedness. They must bear their sin and die childless.
If a man marries his brother's wife, it is wrongdoing, because he has exposed his brother's nakedness. They shall be childless.
Keep all my commandments and my judgments, and carry them out, so that the land into which I am bringing you to live will not vomit you out.
Do not follow the customs of the nations that I am driving out before you, because they did all these things, and I was disgusted with them.
I told you that you would inherit their land. I will give it to you, and you will possess it—a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the Lord your God, who has set you apart from the nations.

Distinguish between clean and unclean animals, and between clean and unclean birds. Do not make yourselves unclean through animals, birds, or any creature that crawls on the ground that I have set apart for you as unclean.
You shall be holy, because I, the Lord, am holy. I have set you apart from the nations to belong to me.
A man or woman who has a familiar spirit or divining spirits must be put to death. They must be stoned, and their blood will be on their own heads.
The Lord said to Moses: Tell the priests, the sons of Aaron, that they must not make themselves unclean through a dead person among their people.
except for a close relative: his father, his mother, his son, his daughter, or his brother,
or his virgin sister who is close to him and has not married a man. For her he may make himself unclean.
He must not make himself unclean for a leader of his people and so defile himself.
They must not shave bald patches on their heads, shave the edges of their beards, or make cuts in their bodies.
Instead, they must be holy to their God and must not defile the name of their God, because they present the Lord’s offerings, the food of their God. They must be holy.
They must not marry a woman who is a prostitute or is defiled, and they must not marry a woman divorced from her husband, because the priest is holy to his God.
You must treat him as holy, because he presents the food of your God. He must be holy to you, because he is holy. I am the Lord who makes you holy.
When a priest’s daughter begins to prostitute herself, she defiles her father. She shall be burned with fire.

The priest who is chief among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been ordained to wear the sacred garments, must not let his hair hang loose or tear his garments.
He must not go in where there is any dead person, nor defile himself for his father or his mother.
He must not leave the sanctuary or defile the sanctuary of his God, because the crown of his God’s anointing oil is upon him. I am the Lord.
He must marry a virgin.
He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, or a woman defiled by prostitution—none of these. Instead, he must marry a virgin from his own people.
He must not defile his offspring among his people, because I am the Lord who makes him holy.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
Speak to Aaron and tell him: Throughout their generations, no man among your descendants who has a bodily defect may approach to present the food of his God.
No man who has a bodily defect may approach: a man who is lame or blind, has a mutilated nose, or has a torn ear.
or a man who has a broken foot or a broken hand;
Or one who is hunched over or unusually small, whose eyebrows have fallen out, who has impaired vision or a white spot in his eyes, who has leprosy or scaly skin, or who has only one testicle.
No man among the descendants of Aaron the priest who has a bodily defect may approach to present the Lord’s offering. Because he has a defect, he must not approach to present the food of his God.
He may eat the bread of his God, [?] the most holy things, from the holy things.
But he must not go inside the curtain or approach the altar, because he has a bodily defect. He must not defile my sanctuary, because I am the Lord who makes them holy.
Moses told this to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the Israelites.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
Tell Aaron and his sons to keep away from the sacred offerings of the Israelites and not defile my holy name, because they consecrate these offerings to me. I am the Lord.

Tell them: Throughout their generations, if anyone among all your descendants approaches the sacred offerings that the Israelites consecrate to the Lord while he is unclean, that person will be destroyed from before my eyes. I am the Lord.

Any man among Aaron’s descendants who has leprosy or a discharge must not eat the sacred food until he becomes clean. The same applies to anyone who touches anything made unclean by a corpse, or to a man who has an emission of semen.
or a man who touches any crawling creature that makes him unclean, or a person who makes him unclean through any kind of uncleanness—
The person who touches it will be unclean until evening and must not eat the sacred food unless he has washed his body with water.
At sunset he shall become clean, and then he may eat the holy offerings, because they are his food.
He must not eat the carcass of an animal torn by a wild beast, so that he does not become unclean through it. I am the Lord.
They must keep my requirements so that they do not bring sins upon themselves and die because of them, having defiled themselves. I am the Lord who makes them holy.
No outsider may eat a holy offering. A priest’s resident guest or hired worker must not eat a holy offering.
When a priest buys a person with his own money, that person may eat his food. Those born in his household may also eat his food.
If a priest’s daughter marries an outsider, she must not eat any of the holy contributions.
If a priest’s daughter becomes widowed or divorced, has no children, and returns to her father’s house as in her youth, she may eat her father’s food. But no outsider may eat it.
If a man eats sacred food by mistake, he must add one-fifth to it and give the sacred food to the priest.
The Israelites shall not profane the holy offerings that they set apart for the Lord.
They will bear guilt and sins when they eat their sacred offerings, because I am the Lord who makes them holy.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:

Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites, and tell them: Any man of the house of Israel, or of those who turn to me and live in Israel, who presents his offering, whether from any of their vows or any of their freewill offerings that they present to the Lord as a whole burnt offering—
For acceptance, a male without a defect, from the cattle, lambs, or goats.
Do not offer anything with a defect, because it will not be accepted on your behalf.
If a man presents a peace offering to the Lord to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, from cattle or goats, it must be without defect. It will be accepted if it has no defect at all.

You must not offer to the Lord any animal that is blind, broken, mutilated, afflicted with growths, scabby, or covered with sores. You must not place an offering from any of these on the altar for the Lord.
You may offer an ox or a sheep whose ear is torn or whose tail is shortened as a voluntary offering, but it will not be accepted in fulfillment of a vow.
Do not offer to the Lord an animal that has been crushed, slit, or mutilated, and do not do this in your land.
You must not offer any of these as the food of your God even if they come from a foreigner, because they are damaged and have defects. They will not be accepted from you.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
When an ox, a sheep, or a goat is born, it must remain with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day onward, it may be accepted as an offering to the Lord.
Do not slaughter a cow or a sheep together with its young on the same day.
When you sacrifice a thanksgiving offering to the Lord, sacrifice it so that it may be accepted.
It must be eaten that same day. Do not leave any of it until morning. I am the Lord.
Keep my commandments and carry them out. I am the Lord.
You must not profane my holy name, so that I may be held holy among the Israelites. I am the Lord, who makes you holy.
Who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: These are the Lord’s appointed festivals, which you are to proclaim as sacred gatherings; these are my festivals.
You may work for six days, but the seventh day is to be a Sabbath and a rest, holy to the Lord. You must not do any work. It is a Sabbath to the Lord wherever you live.
These are the Lord’s festivals, which you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies at their appointed times.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at twilight, is the Lord’s Passover.
On the fifteenth day of this same month is the Festival of Unleavened Bread to the Lord. You must eat unleavened bread for seven days.
On the first day you shall have a sacred assembly. You must not do any ordinary work.
Present an offering to the Lord for seven days. The seventh day is to be a sacred gathering, and you must not do any ordinary work.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land that I am giving you and reap its harvest, bring a sheaf from the first of your harvest to the priest.
He shall present the sheaf before the Lord so that it may be accepted. After another day, the priest shall present it.
On the day when you set apart the sheaf, offer a year-old lamb without defect as a whole burnt offering to the Lord.
Its grain offering is to be two tenth-measures, from two seahs of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering to the Lord for a pleasing aroma. Its drink offering is to be a quarter of a hin of wine.
You must not eat bread, roasted grain, or crushed grain until this day, until the day when you bring the offering to your God. This is a perpetual law throughout your generations, wherever you live.
Count for yourselves from the day afterward, from the day when you bring the sheaf that is set apart. There are to be seven complete weeks.
Count fifty days, until after the seventh week, and offer fine flour from the new crop to the Lord.
Bring bread from your homes as an offering set apart: two loaves [?], made from two tenth-measures of fine flour. They are to be baked with yeast as firstfruits to the Lord.

Along with the bread, offer seven year-old lambs without defect, one young bull, and two rams. They are to be a whole burnt offering to the Lord, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings, an offering for a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Offer one male goat as a sin offering, and two year-old lambs as a sacrifice of well-being.

The priest is to set them apart together with the bread of the firstfruits as an offering set apart before the Lord, along with the two lambs. They are to be holy before the Lord and belong to the priest.
Proclaim this day as a sacred gathering, and do not do any ordinary work. This is a perpetual law throughout your generations, wherever you live.

When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap the edges of your fields completely, and do not gather the gleanings of your harvest. Instead, leave them for the poor and for those who turn to me. I am the Lord your God.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: On the first day of the seventh month, you are to have a rest and a memorial marked by a proclamation. You are to have a sacred gathering.
You shall do no ordinary work, and you shall bring an offering to the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him: Speak to the Israelites and tell them:
The tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. You are to have a sacred gathering. Humble yourselves and present an offering to the Lord.
You must not do any work on this very day, because it is the Day of Atonement, when atonement is made for you before the Lord your God.
For anyone who does not humble themselves on that day shall perish from among their people.
Anyone who does any work on that day—I will destroy that person from among their people.
You shall do no work. This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations, wherever you live.
It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you must humble yourselves. On the ninth day of the month, in the evening, at twilight, from evening until evening, observe your Sabbaths [?].
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month, celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days before the Lord.
On the first day you shall hold a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.
Seven days. Offer an offering to the Lord. On the eighth day you shall have a holy assembly, and you shall offer an offering to the Lord. You shall gather together, and you shall do no ordinary work.

These are the festivals of the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies, and at which you shall offer offerings to the Lord: whole burnt offerings, fine flour, drink offerings, and sacrifices, each day's required portion on its day.

These are in addition to the Lord's Sabbaths, in addition to your offerings, in addition to your gifts, in addition to all your vows, and in addition to all your voluntary contributions that you give to the Lord.

But on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you gather in the produce of the land, celebrate a festival to the Lord for seven days. On the first day there shall be a cessation from work, and on the eighth day, rest.
On the first day take for yourselves fruit from beautiful trees: citrons, palm branches, myrtle, and willows. Rejoice before the Lord your God for seven days, all you of the house of Israel.
Celebrate this festival to the Lord for seven days each year. It is a lasting statute throughout your generations. Celebrate it in the seventh month.
Live in shelters for seven days. All those of the house of Israel shall live in shelters.
So that your generations may know that I made the Israelites live in shelters when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
Moses told the Israelites about the festivals of the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Command the Israelites to bring you pure, pressed olive oil to keep the lamps burning continually.
Outside the entrance of the testimony, in the tent of meeting, Aaron shall tend them from evening until morning before the Lord continually. This is a lasting statute throughout your generations.
He shall arrange the lamps on the great lampstand before the Lord continually.
Take fine flour and bake twelve cakes [?], each cake [?] made from two-tenths.
Arrange them in two rows, six in each row, on the pure table before the Lord.
Put pure frankincense on the rows before the Lord. It shall serve as a memorial portion for the bread, an offering to the Lord.
On the sixth day Aaron shall arrange them before the Lord regularly, on behalf of the Israelites, as an everlasting covenant.
It shall belong to Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place, because it is most holy for him among the Lord's offerings. This is a lasting statute.
The son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian man, went out among the Israelites. The Israelite woman's son and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
The Israelite woman's son pronounced the Name and cursed. They brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.
They held him in custody so that the Lord’s own word would make the matter clear to them.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Take the man who cursed outside the camp. All who heard him shall lay their hands on his head, and the whole congregation shall stone him.
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: Whenever anyone curses his God, he shall bear his sin.

Whoever pronounces the name of the Lord shall certainly be put to death. The whole congregation shall stone him. Whether someone who has turned to me or an Israelite, when he pronounces my name, he shall be put to death.
If anyone kills a human being, he shall certainly be put to death.
Whoever kills an animal shall make restitution, life for life.
If anyone injures his neighbor, just as he injured his neighbor, so shall it be done to him.
Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As he has inflicted an injury on his neighbor, so it shall be done to him.
Whoever kills an animal shall pay for it, and whoever kills a person shall be put to death.
You shall have one law. It shall be the same for someone who has turned to me and for an Israelite. I am the Lord your God.
Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they took the man who had cursed outside the camp. They stoned him with stones, and he died. The Israelites did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land that I am giving you as an inheritance, the land shall observe a Sabbath to the Lord.
For six years you shall sow your fields, for six years you shall prune your vineyards, and for six years you shall gather in your produce.
But the seventh year shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land, and it shall be a Sabbath to the Lord for you. You shall not sow your fields or prune your vineyards.
You shall not reap what grows by itself from your harvest, nor gather the grapes from your vines. It shall be a year of Sabbath rest for the land.
What the land produces during its Sabbath shall be food for you, for your male and female slaves, for your hired workers, and for the settlers who live with you.
All its produce shall also be food for your livestock and the wild animals in your land.
Count for yourselves seven Sabbaths of years, seven years seven times. The duration of the seven Sabbaths of years shall be forty-nine years.
Sound the trumpet of jubilation on the tenth day of the seventh month. On the Day of Atonement, sound the trumpet throughout your land.

Set apart the fiftieth year as holy, and proclaim freedom throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a Jubilee for you. Each of you shall return to his inherited property, and each to his family.
The fiftieth year shall be a Jubilee for you. You must not sow your land, reap what grows on its own, or gather grapes from its vines.
For it is a Jubilee and shall be holy to you. Eat the produce directly from the fields.
In this year of Jubilee, each of you shall return to his ancestral property.
If you sell something to your neighbor or buy something from your neighbor, do not wrong one another.
Buy from your neighbor according to the number of years since the Jubilee, and he shall sell to you according to the number of years of harvest.
When there are more years, you shall increase its purchase price, and when there are fewer years, you shall reduce its purchase price, because what he is selling you is a number of annual harvests.
Do not wrong one another, but fear your God, for I am the Lord your God.
Carry out my commandments, and keep my laws and obey them. Then you shall live securely in the land.
The land shall yield its fruit, and you shall eat your fill and live securely in it.
If you say, “What shall we eat in the seventh year, since we will neither sow nor gather its produce?”
I will send you my blessings in the sixth year, and it shall produce a harvest sufficient for three years.
You shall sow in the eighth year and eat from the old harvest until the ninth year. Until the harvest comes in, you shall continue eating the old produce.
The land must certainly not be sold permanently, because the land is mine, and you are foreigners and temporary residents with me.
Throughout all the land you hold as your inheritance, you must allow the land to be redeemed.
If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his inherited property, his nearest relative shall come and redeem what his brother sold.
If there is no one to redeem it, but he gains the means and finds enough to redeem it,
he shall calculate the years since its sale and return the remaining value to the man who bought it from him. Then he shall return to his ancestral property.

If he does not have enough to repay the buyer, the sale shall remain valid for the one who bought it until the year of Jubilee. At the Jubilee it shall be released, and he shall return to his inherited property.
If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled town, he shall have the right to redeem it until a year from its sale is completed. His right to redeem it shall last from one season to the same season.

If it is not redeemed before a full year has passed, the house in the walled town shall belong permanently to the one who bought it and shall pass to his descendants. It shall not be released from his possession at the Jubilee.
But houses in open settlements that have no surrounding wall shall be regarded as fields in the countryside. They shall be subject to redemption and shall be released at the Jubilee.
As for the towns of the Levites and the houses in the towns belonging to them, the Levites shall always have the right to redeem them.

If anyone redeems property from the Levites, the sale of the house and the town of his inherited property shall be released at the Jubilee, because the houses in the Levites’ towns are their inherited property among the Israelites.
The fields on the outskirts of their towns must not be sold, because they are their permanent possession.
If your brother becomes poor and his means fail, you must not hold him with you as a foreigner or a temporary resident. He shall live with you.
Do not take interest or profit from him. Fear your God, and let your brother live with you.
Do not lend him your money at interest or give him your food for profit.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
If your brother becomes poor and is sold to you, do not make him do the work of a slave.
He shall be with you as a hired worker or a temporary resident. He shall remain with you until the year of Jubilee.
He shall leave you, he and his children with him, and return to his family. He shall return to his father’s inherited property.
For they are my slaves, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They must not be sold as slaves are sold.
Do not make him work harshly, but fear your God.
The male and female slaves you own shall come from the nations around you. From them you may buy male and female slaves.
You may also acquire slaves from the children of the temporary residents who live with you, and from their families living among you who were born in your land. They shall become your property.

You may pass them on to your children after you as inherited property, and you may make them work for you permanently. But you must not make your brothers, the Israelites, perform harsh labor, one brother for another.

If a foreigner or temporary resident living with you gains sufficient means, and your brother living beside him becomes poor and sells himself to the foreigner or temporary resident living with you, or to someone born into the family of the foreigner living with you,
he shall have the right to be redeemed after he has been sold. One of his brothers may redeem him.
his uncle or his uncle’s son may redeem him, or a close blood relative from his family may redeem him. If he gains sufficient means, he may redeem himself.

He shall calculate with his buyer the time from the year he sold himself to him until the year of Jubilee. The price of his sale shall be reckoned according to the number of years. His time with the buyer shall be reckoned like the days of a hired worker.
If many years still remain, he shall pay back his redemption price in proportion to them, based on the money paid for him.
If only a few years remain until the year of Jubilee, he shall calculate with him and repay his redemption price in proportion to those years.
He shall be with him as a worker hired year by year. His owner must not make him work harshly before your eyes.
If he is not redeemed by these means, he shall go free in the year of Jubilee, together with his children.
For the Israelites belong to me as slaves. They are my slaves, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
Do not make idols or images for yourselves, and do not set up sacred pillars for yourselves. Do not make stones for worship in your land, and do not bow down to them. I myself am the LORD your God.
Keep my commandments and revere my sanctuary. I am the Lord.
If you follow my laws, keep my commandments, and carry them out,
I will give you rain at its proper times. The land will yield its produce, and the trees of the field will bear their fruit.
Your threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will last until sowing time. You will eat your bread and be satisfied, and you will live peacefully in your land.
I will give peace in your land. You will lie down, and no one will frighten you. I will rid the land of dangerous animals, and no sword will pass through your land.
You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand. Your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
I will turn toward you, make you increase, and multiply you. I will establish my covenant with you.
You will eat food from stores long kept, and you will clear out the old to make room for the new.
I will place my dwelling among you, and I will not detest you.
I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be my people.
I myself am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be their slaves. I broke the yoke of your slavery and made you walk upright.
But if you do not listen to me and do not carry out all these commandments,
If you reject my laws, despise my judgments, fail to carry out all my commandments, and break my covenants,

then I too will do this to you: I will bring terror upon you, leprosy, scaly skin disease, and dysentery that wears out the eyes and drains away life. You will sow your seed in vain, and your enemies will eat it.
I will turn my anger against you, and you will be defeated before your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee even when no one is pursuing you.
If even after these things you do not listen to me, I will punish you sevenfold for your sins.
I will break your proud strength. I will make your skies like iron and your land like bronze.
Your strength will be exhausted in vain. Your land will not yield its crops, and the trees of the land will not yield their fruit.
If you act with hostility toward me and are unwilling to obey me, I will bring seven times more plagues upon you for your sins.
I will send wild animals against you, and they will rob you of your children, destroy your livestock, and reduce your numbers. Your roads will become deserted.
If even after these things you will not accept correction, but act with hostility toward me,
then I too will act with hostility toward you, and I myself will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
I will bring a sword against you to exact vengeance for the covenant. You will flee to your towns, and I will send a plague among you. You will be handed over to your enemies.
I will cut off your supply of grain. Ten women will bake your bread in one oven, and they will give you bread rationed by weight. You will eat but will not be satisfied.
If even after these things you do not listen to me, but act with hostility toward me,
I too will deal with you in anger and hostility, and I will punish you sevenfold for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons, and you will eat the flesh of your daughters.
I will lay waste your shrines and destroy your idols. I will throw your corpses onto the corpses of your idols, and I will despise you.
I will turn your towns into ruins and lay your sanctuary waste. I will not smell your pleasing fragrance.
I myself will lay the land waste, and your enemies who live in it will be appalled at it.
I will scatter you among the nations and draw a sword after you. Your land will become a wasteland, and your towns will become ruins.
Then the land will enjoy its Sabbath rests throughout the time it lies desolate, while you are in the land of your enemies. Then the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
Throughout the time it lies desolate, it will rest, because it did not rest during your Sabbaths when you lived in it.

As for those of you who remain, I will put terror in their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a rustling leaf will send them fleeing. They will flee as people flee from a sword, and they will fall when no one is pursuing them.
They will stumble over one another as though fleeing from a sword, even though no one is pursuing them. They will have no strength to stand before their enemies.
You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will devour you.
Those of you who remain will waste away because of their wrongdoing in the land of their enemies. They will also waste away because of their ancestors’ wrongdoing.
They will confess their wrongdoing and the wrongdoing of their ancestors—the wrong they committed against me and the hostility with which they treated me.

I too will act with hostility toward them and bring them into the land of their enemies. Then their uncircumcised hearts will be humbled, and then they will accept the punishment for their wrongdoing.
I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and my covenant with Isaac. I will remember my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.

The land will be abandoned by them and will enjoy its Sabbath rests while it lies desolate without them. They will accept the punishment for their wrongdoing because they rejected my judgments and despised my commandments.
Even when they were in the land of their enemies, I did not reject them or cast them away. I did not destroy them, and I did not break my covenant with them.

But I remembered for their sake the covenant with their ancestors, because I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations and became their God. I am the Lord.
These are the commandments, laws, and judgments that the Lord established between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai through Moses.
The LORD spoke with Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When someone makes a special vow to the Lord based on the assessed value of persons,
the assessed value of a male from twenty years old up to sixty years old shall be fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel.
If it is a female, her assessed value shall be thirty shekels.
If the person is from five years old up to twenty years old, the assessed value of a male shall be twenty shekels, and that of a female ten shekels.
If the person is from one month old up to five years old, the assessed value of a male shall be five shekels of silver, and that of a female three shekels of silver.
If it is a male sixty years old or older, his assessed value shall be fifteen shekels, and that of a female ten shekels.

If he is too poor to pay the assessed value, he shall be brought before the priest, and the priest shall determine his value. The priest shall determine his value according to what the person who made the vow can afford.
If it is an animal of a kind offered as an offering to the Lord, whatever anyone gives to the Lord shall be holy.
It must not be exchanged, a good one for a bad one or a bad one for a good one. If someone does exchange one animal for another, both it and its replacement shall be holy to the Lord.
If it is an unclean animal of a kind not offered as an offering to the Lord, the animal shall be brought before the priest.
The priest shall assess its value according to whether it is good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets shall stand.
If he redeems it, he shall add one-fifth to its value.
If someone dedicates his house as holy to the Lord, the priest shall assess its value according to whether it is good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets shall stand.
If the person who dedicated his house redeems it, he shall add one-fifth of its assessed value in silver, and it shall be his.

If someone dedicates to the Lord part of a field that he inherited, its assessed value shall be in proportion to the seed needed to sow it: fifty shekels of silver for land requiring a kor of barley seed.
If he dedicates his field from the year of Jubilee, its full valuation shall stand.
If he dedicates his field after the Jubilee, the priest shall calculate the silver due from him in proportion to the years remaining until the Jubilee year, and reduce its assessed value.
If the person who dedicated the field redeems it, he shall add one-fifth of its assessed value in silver, and it shall be his.
If he does not redeem the field and sells it to another man, it shall no longer be redeemable.
But when the field is released in the Jubilee, it shall be holy to the Lord, like a field irrevocably devoted to him. It shall become the priest’s inherited property.
If the field a man dedicates to the Lord is one he purchased, rather than a field belonging to his inheritance,
The priest shall calculate its assessed value up to the Jubilee year, and he shall pay its assessed value that day as a holy offering to the Lord.
In the Jubilee year, the field shall return to the person from whom it was purchased, the one to whom the land belongs as inherited property.
All its valuations shall be in shekels. A shekel is twenty gerahs.
But no one may dedicate a firstborn animal that already belongs to the Lord as a firstborn. Whether it is an ox or a lamb, it belongs to the Lord.
If it is an unclean animal, it shall be redeemed at its assessed value, with one-fifth added to it. If it is not redeemed, it shall be sold at its assessed value.

But anything that someone irrevocably devotes to the Lord from all that he owns, whether a person, an animal, or a field that he inherited, must not be sold or redeemed. Everything irrevocably devoted is most holy to the Lord.
No person who has been irrevocably devoted shall be redeemed; that person must be put to death.
Every tithe of the land, whether from the crops of the land or from the fruit of the trees, belongs to the Lord and is holy to the Lord.
If a man redeems any of his tithe, he shall add one-fifth to it.
Every tithe of cattle and sheep, from all that passes under the shepherd’s rod, shall be holy to the Lord.
He must not inquire whether it is good or bad, or bad or good. He must not exchange it. If he does exchange it, both it and its substitute will be holy, and it must not be redeemed.
These are the commandments that the Lord gave Moses concerning the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
